Table S13.2

Attempted and usable percentile-bootstrap resamples of every bootstrap analysis in each sample

Primary sample Sensitivity sample
Record Attempted Usable Minimum Attempted Usable Minimum
Note. Each row is one record of bootstrap attempts: one record for all versions of a structural or threshold model (an attempt is usable only when every version succeeds), or a record per version of the other bootstrap analyses; for the search-target thresholds (E15g), the usable resamples that cross the threshold. Usable = attempted minus failed. Minimum: met when usable reaches the minimum of 9,500 (the registered rule for a decision); below it the analysis is incomplete and its intervals carry no decision. Analyses without a bootstrap (the analyses of covariance, the repeated-measures and multilevel models, the generalized estimating equations and the moderation models) have no attempt record.

Table S13.3

Each letter’s registered targets and decisions in the primary and the sensitivity samples

Primary sample Sensitivity sample
Letter and target Estimate 95% CI Decision Estimate 95% CI Decision Verdict differs
Note. One row per letter and per target its registered decision rule reads under the primary legal-context set, with the estimate and interval of the table that rule reads; decimals follow each row's magnitude. A directional letter is supported when its interval lies on the predicted side of zero, an equivalence letter when its interval lies inside the registered bounds. Verdict differs: yes when the two samples give different verdicts (supported, not supported); — when either sample gives none (unavailable, reported without a verdict, or suppressed). No test compares the samples. H3c, H3d, H3e: substitute mediator: pregnancy-evidence likelihood; deviation 2 in S1. Each row's interval uses its letter's registered procedure. Prefixes Ab and Di name the illegal-abortion and improper-disposal contexts, pooled the legal contexts pooled, Ab_minus_Di or Ab_Di their difference; no prefix, the contexts averaged with equal weights. XS and SMA = expected evidence, XF and Financial = unexpected evidence, None = no information; A_B = A minus B. Expected evidence = evidence consistent with a self-managed abortion; unexpected evidence = financial-crime evidence. n per condition, primary sample: Illegal abortion: No information 68, Expected evidence 63, Unexpected evidence 63; Improper disposal: No information 71, Expected evidence 66, Unexpected evidence 67 (all 398 in the analysis). n per condition, sensitivity sample: Illegal abortion: No information 55, Expected evidence 56, Unexpected evidence 54; Improper disposal: No information 56, Expected evidence 62, Unexpected evidence 58 (all 341 in the analysis).

Every saved comparison of the RQ1 analyses in the primary and the sensitivity samples

Primary sample Sensitivity sample
Estimand Estimate 95% CI n Estimate 95% CI n Interval
Note. Every saved comparison of each registered version of the RQ1 analyses, in each sample; each band is one analysis and version (registered model = the model the decision rules read; the other versions are its registered companions). Decimals follow each row's magnitude. n = the participants in the model of that version and sample. 95% intervals by each row's saved procedure (Interval): percentile bootstrap (participant resamples, stratified within the six conditions); Wald from the robust or heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) covariance, or from the joint normal maximum-likelihood covariance; Student t or Satterthwaite t for the linear models; — where the saved comparison has no interval (E14a's threshold differences, whose confidence sets are in its own files). No test compares the samples. Percentile-bootstrap resamples behind the bootstrap intervals of this table, over the attempt records of its analyses: primary sample, 10,000 attempted and 10,000 usable; sensitivity sample, 10,000 attempted and 10,000 usable. Each record is in the table of bootstrap attempts in S13. Prefixes Ab and Di name the illegal-abortion and improper-disposal contexts, pooled the legal contexts pooled, Ab_minus_Di or Ab_Di their difference; no prefix, the contexts averaged with equal weights. XS and SMA = expected evidence, XF and Financial = unexpected evidence, None = no information; A_B = A minus B. n per condition, primary sample: Illegal abortion: No information 68, Expected evidence 63, Unexpected evidence 63; Improper disposal: No information 71, Expected evidence 66, Unexpected evidence 67 (all 398 in the analysis). n per condition, sensitivity sample: Illegal abortion: No information 55, Expected evidence 56, Unexpected evidence 54; Improper disposal: No information 56, Expected evidence 62, Unexpected evidence 58 (all 341 in the analysis).

Table S13.5

Every saved comparison of the RQ2 analyses in the primary and the sensitivity samples

Primary sample Sensitivity sample
Estimand Estimate 95% CI n Estimate 95% CI n Interval
Note. Every saved comparison of each registered version of the RQ2 analyses, in each sample; each band is one analysis and version (registered model = the model the decision rules read; the other versions are its registered companions). Decimals follow each row's magnitude. n = the participants in the model of that version and sample. 95% intervals by each row's saved procedure (Interval): percentile bootstrap (participant resamples, stratified within the six conditions); Wald from the robust or heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) covariance, or from the joint normal maximum-likelihood covariance; Student t or Satterthwaite t for the linear models; — where the saved comparison has no interval (E14a's threshold differences, whose confidence sets are in its own files). No test compares the samples. Percentile-bootstrap resamples behind the bootstrap intervals of this table, over the attempt records of its analyses: primary sample, 10,000 attempted and 10,000 usable; sensitivity sample, 10,000 attempted and 10,000 usable. Each record is in the table of bootstrap attempts in S13. Prefixes Ab and Di name the illegal-abortion and improper-disposal contexts, pooled the legal contexts pooled, Ab_minus_Di or Ab_Di their difference; no prefix, the contexts averaged with equal weights. XS and SMA = expected evidence, XF and Financial = unexpected evidence, None = no information; A_B = A minus B. n per condition, primary sample: Illegal abortion: No information 68, Expected evidence 63, Unexpected evidence 63; Improper disposal: No information 71, Expected evidence 66, Unexpected evidence 67 (all 398 in the analysis). n per condition, sensitivity sample: Illegal abortion: No information 55, Expected evidence 56, Unexpected evidence 54; Improper disposal: No information 56, Expected evidence 62, Unexpected evidence 58 (all 341 in the analysis).

Every saved comparison of the RQ3 analyses in the primary and the sensitivity samples

Primary sample Sensitivity sample
Estimand Estimate 95% CI n Estimate 95% CI n Interval
Note. Every saved comparison of each registered version of the RQ3 analyses, in each sample; each band is one analysis and version (registered model = the model the decision rules read; the other versions are its registered companions). Decimals follow each row's magnitude. n = the participants in the model of that version and sample. 95% intervals by each row's saved procedure (Interval): percentile bootstrap (participant resamples, stratified within the six conditions); Wald from the robust or heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) covariance, or from the joint normal maximum-likelihood covariance; Student t or Satterthwaite t for the linear models; — where the saved comparison has no interval (E14a's threshold differences, whose confidence sets are in its own files). No test compares the samples. Percentile-bootstrap resamples behind the bootstrap intervals of this table, over the attempt records of its analyses: primary sample, 10,000 attempted and 10,000 usable; sensitivity sample, 10,000 attempted and 10,000 usable. Each record is in the table of bootstrap attempts in S13. Prefixes Ab and Di name the illegal-abortion and improper-disposal contexts, pooled the legal contexts pooled, Ab_minus_Di or Ab_Di their difference; no prefix, the contexts averaged with equal weights. XS and SMA = expected evidence, XF and Financial = unexpected evidence, None = no information; A_B = A minus B. n per condition, primary sample: Illegal abortion: No information 68, Expected evidence 63, Unexpected evidence 63; Improper disposal: No information 71, Expected evidence 66, Unexpected evidence 67 (all 398 in the analysis). n per condition, sensitivity sample: Illegal abortion: No information 55, Expected evidence 56, Unexpected evidence 54; Improper disposal: No information 56, Expected evidence 62, Unexpected evidence 58 (all 341 in the analysis).

Table S13.7

Every saved comparison of the RQ4 analyses in the primary and the sensitivity samples

Primary sample Sensitivity sample
Estimand Estimate 95% CI n Estimate 95% CI n Interval
Note. Every saved comparison of each registered version of the RQ4 analyses, in each sample; each band is one analysis and version (registered model = the model the decision rules read; the other versions are its registered companions). Decimals follow each row's magnitude. n = the participants in the model of that version and sample. 95% intervals by each row's saved procedure (Interval): percentile bootstrap (participant resamples, stratified within the six conditions); Wald from the robust or heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) covariance, or from the joint normal maximum-likelihood covariance; Student t or Satterthwaite t for the linear models; — where the saved comparison has no interval (E14a's threshold differences, whose confidence sets are in its own files). No test compares the samples. Percentile-bootstrap resamples behind the bootstrap intervals of this table, over the attempt records of its analyses: primary sample, 10,000 attempted and 9,919 to 10,000 usable; sensitivity sample, 10,000 attempted and 9,662 to 10,000 usable. Each record is in the table of bootstrap attempts in S13. Prefixes Ab and Di name the illegal-abortion and improper-disposal contexts, pooled the legal contexts pooled, Ab_minus_Di or Ab_Di their difference; no prefix, the contexts averaged with equal weights. XS and SMA = expected evidence, XF and Financial = unexpected evidence, None = no information; A_B = A minus B. n per condition, primary sample: Illegal abortion: No information 68, Expected evidence 63, Unexpected evidence 63; Improper disposal: No information 71, Expected evidence 66, Unexpected evidence 67 (all 398 in the analysis). n per condition, sensitivity sample: Illegal abortion: No information 55, Expected evidence 56, Unexpected evidence 54; Improper disposal: No information 56, Expected evidence 62, Unexpected evidence 58 (all 341 in the analysis).

Table S13.8

Every saved comparison of the RQ5 analyses in the primary and the sensitivity samples

Primary sample Sensitivity sample
Estimand Estimate 95% CI n Estimate 95% CI n Interval
Note. Every saved comparison of each registered version of the RQ5 analyses, in each sample; each band is one analysis and version (registered model = the model the decision rules read; the other versions are its registered companions). Decimals follow each row's magnitude. n = the participants in the model of that version and sample. 95% intervals by each row's saved procedure (Interval): percentile bootstrap (participant resamples, stratified within the six conditions); Wald from the robust or heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) covariance, or from the joint normal maximum-likelihood covariance; Student t or Satterthwaite t for the linear models; — where the saved comparison has no interval (E14a's threshold differences, whose confidence sets are in its own files). No test compares the samples. No analysis in this table has a percentile-bootstrap interval. Note. Decimals follow each row's magnitude. n = the participants in the model of that version and sample. 95% intervals by each row's saved procedure (Interval): percentile bootstrap (participant resamples, stratified within the six conditions); Wald from the robust or heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) covariance, or from the joint normal maximum-likelihood covariance; Student t or Satterthwaite t for the linear models; — where the saved comparison has no interval (E14a's threshold differences, whose confidence sets are in its own files). No test compares the samples.
